prompt: Write the third selected column: the highest committed offset for each partition, or 0 when nobody has committed. Use COALESCE around MAX(c.committed_offset) with 0 as the fallback, and name the column best with AS.
given: Query: SELECT p.topic, p.partition_id, <your column> FROM partitions p LEFT JOIN commits c ... GROUP BY p.topic, p.partition_id
template:
-- EXPECTED: [["audit", 0, 10], ["empty", 0, 0], ["orders", 0, 100], ["orders", 1, 210], ["payments", 0, 40]]

-- Tables are loaded for you: partitions(topic, partition_id, log_end_offset) and commits(group_id, topic, partition_id, committed_offset).
SELECT p.topic, p.partition_id,
       @@BLANK@@
FROM partitions p
LEFT JOIN commits c ON c.topic = p.topic AND c.partition_id = p.partition_id
GROUP BY p.topic, p.partition_id
ORDER BY p.topic, p.partition_id;
why: COALESCE replaces NULL with a fallback value, so partitions with no commits show 0.
